titre: The Hays Code went four years without censoring anything
accroche: Adopted in 1930, the Hays Code wasn't actually enforced until July 1934, under the threat of a Catholic boycott.
contenu_vulgarise:
In 1930, the Hollywood studios, united in the Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America (MPPDA), adopt a detailed code of conduct, drafted to head off any state censorship after a series of resounding scandals. The text, later called the Hays Code after its president Will Hays, bans in black and white drug trafficking, prostitution, sex between white and Black people, and kisses judged too lascivious.

## Four years without a single sanction

The Code, however, provides no mechanism to make itself obeyed. From 1930 to 1934, the studios keep producing what will be called pre-Code cinema afterward: Scarface and Little Caesar make their gangsters almost admirable characters, Baby Face features a woman who climbs the ranks of a New York bank by seducing, one after another, the men who can promote her. The Code exists, but nothing forces anyone to comply.

The situation shifts in 1934. Catholic prelates found the Legion of Decency, which rates films and calls for boycotts of those it judges indecent. Weakened by the Great Depression, the studios cannot afford to lose the Catholic audience. Hays then creates the Production Code Administration (PCA), tasked with examining every script and every final print, and puts Joseph Breen in charge. From July 1, 1934, no major studio distributes a film without its seal of approval. The first to get it is The World Moves On, by John Ford.

Enforcement, this time, is real: on Casablanca, in 1942, Breen's office requires that the Nazi officer Strasser fire first, so that Bogart doesn't shoot him in the back. Yet it lets negotiated exceptions slip through: in 1939, the word “damn,” explicitly proscribed by the Code, stays in the last line of Gone with the Wind after the producer David O. Selznick obtains a waiver.

## What this shifts

The Hays Code that we imagine shaped American cinema from 1930 on therefore censored nothing at all for four years. What really changed the content of Hollywood films was not a text. It was a specific economic threat, carried by a Church capable of mobilizing part of the public in the midst of a crisis. Pre-Code cinema, rediscovered today as a surprisingly free interlude, owes its name, moreover, only to what followed it: no one at the time knew they were living in a before.

citation.texte: No picture shall be produced which will lower the moral standards of those who see it. Hence the sympathy of the audience shall never be thrown to the side of crime, wrongdoing, evil, or sin.
citation.source: Original 1930 text, quoted by Encyclopaedia Britannica

carte.punch: The Hays Code, adopted in 1930, censored nothing at all before the summer of 1934.
carte.idee: Adopted in 1930, the Hays Code provides no mechanism to make itself obeyed: pre-Code cinema allows itself admirable gangsters and liberated women. It takes the threat of a Catholic boycott, in 1934, for a dedicated administration to finally enforce the Code, film by film.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The complete history of the Code, from its adoption in 1930 to its replacement by the rating system in 1968.

quiz.question: What truly changed the content of Hollywood films from 1934 on, when the Hays Code had existed since 1930?
choix: A federal law passed by the U.S. Congress making the Code mandatory on pain of a fine
The creation of the Production Code Administration, under the threat of a boycott organized by the Catholic Legion of Decency
The replacement of Will Hays by a stricter censor at the head of the MPPDA
The arrival of talking pictures, which supposedly made dialogue easier to monitor
quiz.explication: From 1930 to 1934, the Hays Code came with no sanction mechanism, hence the period known as pre-Code cinema. It was the threat of a boycott organized by the Legion of Decency, Catholic prelates worried about the influence of movies, that pushed the studios, weakened by the Great Depression, to create the Production Code Administration and put Joseph Breen in charge.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which film was the first to receive the seal of the brand-new Production Code Administration, on July 1, 1934?
choix: The World Moves On, by John Ford
Gone with the Wind, by Victor Fleming
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text names The World Moves On, by John Ford, as the first film to receive the PCA seal from July 1, 1934, the date the Code actually took effect.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What did Joseph Breen's office require on the making of Casablanca, in 1942?
choix: That Bogart's character kill Strasser without a confrontation
That the scene be cut from the film outright
That the Nazi officer Strasser fire first, so that Bogart doesn't shoot him in the back
That the character of Strasser be replaced by an unidentified civilian not marked as a Nazi
quiz_supplementaire.explication: On Casablanca, in 1942, Breen's office required that the officer Strasser fire first, so that Bogart's shot would look like a response rather than a murder in the back.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why did the word damn, explicitly proscribed by the Code, stay in the last line of Gone with the Wind in 1939?
choix: Because the film came out before the Code actually took effect in 1934
Because the producer David O. Selznick obtained a specific waiver
Because Joseph Breen had meanwhile removed the word from the list of banned terms
Because a court ruled, on appeal, that the word fell outside the Code
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text specifies that the producer David O. Selznick obtained a waiver allowing him to keep the word damn, despite its explicit prohibition by the Hays Code.
